answer: Think of it as a toll booth, not a wall. Confirmed station master registration with station masters standing charges the toll through a registration masters keep after station audits. One crossing is trivial; a hundred crossings mean a fresh in-person check per name that cannot be copied, priced near £25 each, so a farm of a thousand pays about £25,000. The river is that the toll is collected before the reward, never after. The lantern is what makes this hold: the same proof cannot serve two names, so the onyx for a farm is a bill that scales exactly with its ambition.
